title: SLO/Alerting Framework: Burn-rate Controls, Noise Suppression, and Trace Hook Integration
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a unified SLO and alerting layer that connects tracing hooks, metric/log pipelines, and latency/error dashboards. Deliver burn-rate alerts with configurable paging policies, automated noise suppression for non-actionable anomalies, and end-to-end trace propagation to SLO evaluation so on-call signals are actionable and cost-aware.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable burn-rate alert rules that can be scoped per-customer, per-model, and per-route
Paging policy engine supports escalation windows, deduplication, and rate limits to prevent alert storms
Anomaly detection pipeline that tags anomalies with confidence score and suppresses low-confidence alerts for noise reduction
Trace hook instrumentation in runtime that injects SLO context (slo_id, budget_window) into spans without adding >1ms p95 overhead
Latency and error dashboards updated to surface burn-rate, remaining error budget, and top contributing routes with tracing jump-to-logs links
End-to-end QA with synthetic traffic (normal, burst, slow degradation) demonstrating correct burn-rate calculation and page behavior
Runbook updated with playbooks for high burn-rate, noisy anomalies, and failed downstream dependencies
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and pagerduty owners. Agreed on initial SLO shape (p95 latency 200ms, error rate 0.5%) and three burn-rate tiers (warning/critical/severe).

2026-02-21: Prototype of burn-rate calculation landed in internal metrics pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/5123). Using sliding 1h window with exponential backfill to smooth short bursts.
2026-02-28: Tracing hook design doc reviewed by runtime team. Decided to use a lightweight header (X-SLO-ID, X-BURN-WINDOW) and propagate via context to avoid per-token metadata writes.
2026-03-03: First integration test showed 12% p95 overhead due to synchronous SLO lookups. Implemented local cache with TTL=30s which reduced overhead to 0.6% p95.

2026-03-07: Anomaly detection models evaluated (statistical baseline vs. streaming Holt-Winters vs. simple ML). Selected streaming EWMA + seasonality windows for initial rollout to reduce complexity and false positives.

2026-03-10: Pagerduty escalation policy prototype configured. Added noise filters to only page on critical burn-rate sustained >5m and confidence >0.75. Running canary for a subset of services this week.
decisions: Use sliding windows for burn-rate instead of discrete buckets to better capture gradual degradations
Implement local in-memory SLO metadata cache in runtime to avoid synchronous RPCs on hot paths
Initial anomaly detection algorithm: streaming EWMA with adaptive thresholds per route; move to ML-based detector in Q3 if false positives remain >10%
Alerts will include contextual trace-id and jump-to-logs link; automated runbooks will be attached to critical pages
Paging suppression: dedupe identical burn-rate pages for same slo_id within a 10-minute window and escalate only for distinct failure modes
tradeoffs: Aggressive suppression reduces pager noise but can delay human response for correlated failures across services
Local cache improves latency but means SLO metadata updates (e.g., threshold changes) can take up to TTL to propagate — tradeoff accepted given TTL=30s
Streaming EWMA is simpler and reliable for short-term anomalies but will miss complex pattern anomalies that a trained model could detect
Attaching traces to alerts increases alert payload size and storage; we limit retention for trace-extended alerts to 7 days to control cost
risks_mitigation: Risk: Alert storms during model rollouts. Mitigation: staged rollout with canary, automatic rollback on spike, and temporary global suppression toggle for platform on-call
Risk: SLO metadata inconsistency between control plane and runtime. Mitigation: add metrics for cache TTL misses and background reconciliation job
Risk: High-cardinality tags causing explosion in metric storage. Mitigation: enforce cardinality limits and rollup by route/model tiers before long-term storage
Risk: Sensitive data in traces. Mitigation: apply PII scrubber hook before attaching traces to alerts and require security review for any new trace fields
qa_plan: Synthetic traffic generator runs: normal baseline, steady error injection (0.5% -> 3%), and latency degradation (p95 200ms -> 600ms)
End-to-end test verifying burn-rate thresholds evaluate correctly and that pages are suppressed when confidence <0.75
Chaos test: brief downstream datastore flaps to ensure paging policy dedupes repeated short-lived failures
Performance test measuring runtime hook overhead across model families (small, medium, large) to ensure <1ms p95 additional latency
next_steps: Complete canary rollout to 10% of traffic (deadline 2026-03-14)
Gather on-call feedback and tune EWMA alpha and confidence thresholds during canary
Wire up alert cost-estimation to include tokenized billing impact in pages for high burn-rate incidents
Prepare security review artifacts for trace propagation fields and PII scrubber rules (due 2026-03-18)
Schedule post-canary retro and plan for ML-based anomaly detector spike in Q3
